```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(esc)
library(meta)
library(metafor)
library(dmetar)
library(data.table)

```
#install dmetar here: devtools::install_github("MathiasHarrer/dmetar")

# Calculated Hedge's g given certain statistics
## FOR WHEN studies only report certain statistics and you want to include them
#the ESC library helps us convert any weird study to Hedge's g
#One-way anova


We can also derive the SMD from the F-value of a ANOVA with two groups. Such ANOVAs can be identified by looking at the degrees of freedom. The guide specifically requires it to be a ONE_WAY ANOVA so to be safe only analyze these here.

MUST be one-way AnOVA

Other ANOVAs from a higher order structure can be computed in Psychometrica website

```{r MUST BE ONEWAY ANOVA, Convert to G, given F-value (2 groups), include=FALSE}
library(esc)
esc_f(f = 12.48,      # F value of the one-way anova (2 groups)
      grp1n = 19,   # sample size of group 1 (which is "experimental" does not matter in this calculation) 
      grp2n = 20,   # sample size of group 2
      es.type = "d") # convert to Hedges' g; use "d" for SMD

```


```{r}
#first Cohen's d, total sample size
hedges_g(0.441, 85)

#standard error
#Syntax
#se_g <- sqrt((n1 + n2) / (n1 * n2) + (g^2 / (2 * (n1 + n2))))
se_g <- sqrt(( 41+ 44) / (41 * 44) + (0.441^2 / (2 * (41 + 44))))

```



#given. Means and SDs. First get the standard error
```{r Convert to G, given means, standard error, include=FALSE}
library(esc)
# Compute the standard error first: standard error= standard deviation divided by the sqrt of sample size 
#at https://www.allmath.com/standard-error-calculator.php


esc_mean_se(grp1n = 36,    # sample in group 1
            grp1m = 5.6,   # mean of group 1,exp
            grp1se = 0.13333,  # standard error of group 1
            
            grp2n = 55,    # sample in group 2
            grp2m = -1.9,    # mean of group 2
            grp2se = 0.09439,  # standard error of group 2
          
            es.type = "g") # use "g" for Hedges' g
```

#given p-value and Cohen's D, we can calculate both the SE and hedges G
#this calculation is not consistent with Hedges from Mean/SE
```{r GIVEN p-value and Cohen's d, include=FALSE}
#first effect size, then, pvalue, then total sample size
se.from.p(0.9,
          p = 0.007,
          N = 40,
          effect.size.type = "difference",
           calculate.g=TRUE)
```


```{r Convert to G, given a t-test}
esc_t(t = 4.03,     # t-value 
      grp1n = 41, # sample size of group1 ('which is experimental and which is control won't matter)
      grp2n = 44, # sample size of group 2
      es.type="g") # convert to SMD; use "g" for Hedges' g
```

#Independent two-sample t-test
```{r Convert to G, given indp. two-sample, include=FALSE}
esc_t(t = 6.86,     # t-value 
      grp1n = 27, # sample size of group1
      grp2n = 27, # sample size of group 2
      es.type="g") # convert to SMD; use "g" for Hedges' g

```

#Inputs: pre-calculated Hedges'g (format: csv)
#explanation: We inputHedge's g data we just calculated into a CSV and feed that 
into our meta-gen object. 
```{r  Input, include=FALSE}
#takes any 
library(data.table)

#load data
AnxietyDecis <- fread (file = "/Users/juanbalcazar/Downloads/PreCal_HedgesG_Meta - Anxiety and Decison-making(5).csv")

AnxietyFlex <- fread(file = "/Users/juanbalcazar/Downloads/PreCal_HedgesG_Meta - Anxiety and Cognitive Flexiblity(4).csv")

DepressDecis <- fread(file = "/Users/juanbalcazar/Downloads/PreCal_HedgesG_Meta - Depression and Decision-making(5).csv")

DepressFlex <- fread(file = "/Users/juanbalcazar/Downloads/PreCal_HedgesG_Meta - Depression and Cognitive Flexibility(4).csv")

Subgroup_Flex <- fread(file = "/Users/juanbalcazar/Downloads/PreCal_HedgesG_Meta - Subgroup- Flexibility(1).csv")

Subgroup_Decis <- fread(file = "/Users/juanbalcazar/Downloads/PreCal_HedgesG_Meta - Subgroup- Decision-making(4).csv")
```


Anxiety and Decision-making
```{r  Calculation: Calculate Pooled Hedges g pre-calculated Hedges G, include=FALSE}
## Anxiety and decision-making
m.gen <- metagen(TE = TE,
                 seTE = seTE,
                 studlab = Author,
                 data = AnxietyDecis,
                 sm = "SMD", #label (the effect sizes are already SMD, but we can give it a a label)
                 random = TRUE, #random effects model
                 fixed = FALSE,
                 method.tau = "REML", #best for continuous outcomes
                 method.random.ci = "HK", # Knapp-Hartung adjustment: reduce the risk of a false positive result.
                 title = "Anxiety and Decision-making")


m.gen <- update(m.gen, prediction = TRUE)
m.gen

# find outliers
Outliers_Anxiety_Dec<-
find.outliers(m.gen)
Outliers_Anxiety_Dec

#egger's test for funnel plot assymetry
eggers.test(m.gen)

```

Anxiety and Cognitive Flexiblity

```{r  Calculation: Calculate Pooled Hedges g pre-calculated Hedges G, include=FALSE}

m.gen_anxFlex <- metagen(TE = TE,
```

Compare the pooled effects, using apriori fixed effects (anxiety, depression)

```{r  Subgroup Analysis, include=FALSE}
#subgroup-Flexibility
subgroupFlex <- metagen(TE = TE,
                 seTE = seTE,
                 studlab = Author,
                 data = Subgroup_Flex,
                 sm = "SMD", #label (the effect sizes are already SMD, but we can give it a a label)
                 random = TRUE, #random effects model
                 fixed = FALSE,
                 subgroup = Subgroup,
                 method.tau = "REML", #best for continuous outccomes
                 method.random.ci = "HK", # Knapp-Hartung adjustment: reduce the risk of a false positive result.
                 title = "Subgroup Analysis, Flexibility")
subgroupFlex

#subgroup-decison-making
subgroupDecis<- metagen(TE = TE,
                 seTE = seTE,
                 studlab = Author,
                 data = Subgroup_Decis,
                 sm = "SMD", #label (the effect sizes are already SMD, but we can give it a a label)
                 random = TRUE, #random effects model
                 fixed = FALSE,
                 subgroup = Subgroup,
                 method.tau = "REML", #best for continuous outccomes
                 method.random.ci = "HK", # Knapp-Hartung adjustment: reduce the risk of a false positive result.
                 title = "Subgroup Analysis, Decision-making")
subgroupDecis
```


Create Forest plots from each metagen object
Take this code and run it in an Rscript, if you want the plots not in the chunks


Anxiety Decison making
```{r}
#remove outliers and then plot
clean_dataAnxietyDecis <- AnxietyDecis[!(AnxietyDecis$Author %in% Outliers_Anxiety_Dec$out.study.random), ]

Cleanm.gen_anxietyDecis <- metagen(TE = TE,
                 seTE = seTE,
                 studlab = Author,
                 data = clean_dataAnxietyDecis,
                 sm = "SMD", #label (the effect sizes are already SMD, but we can give it a a label)
                 random = TRUE, #random effects model
                 fixed = FALSE,
                 method.tau = "REML", #best for continuous outccomes
                 method.random.ci = "HK", # Knapp-Hartung adjustment: reduce the risk of a false positive result.
                 title = "Anxiety and Decision-making")

Cleanm.gen_anxietyDecis  <- update(Cleanm.gen_anxietyDecis, prediction = TRUE)
Cleanm.gen_anxietyDecis

#plot without outliers
plotCleanAnxDecis <- forest(
  Cleanm.gen_anxietyDecis,
  sortvar = TE,  # Sort the studies based on effect size
  prediction = TRUE,  # Add prediction interval
  print.tau2 = FALSE,  # Do not print the heterogeneity measure
  leftcols = c("studlab", "effect", "seTE"),  # Columns for study labels, effect sizes, and standard errors
  leftlabs = c("Author", "g", "SE"),  # Custom labels for the left columns
  rightcols = c("ci", "w.random"),  # Columns for confidence interval and weights (removes 'effect' from right)
  label.left = "Negative numbers reflect deficit vs. controls",  # Custom label for left side of the plot
  smlab = "Effect size g (k= 18)",  # Custom summary label with more context
  col.diamond = "lightblue",  # Lighter cyan for the diamond (summary effect size)
  col.diamond.lines = "black",  # Line color for the diamond
  col.square = "lightgreen",  # Lighter green for individual study squares
  col.square.lines = "black",  # Color for individual square lines
  fontsize = 14,  # Increase font size for better readability
  addprediction = TRUE,  # Explicitly add the prediction interval
  xlim = c(-2, 2),  # Adjust x-axis range
  gridlines = TRUE  # Add grid lines for better reference
)

```
